messages.author: a70102b7393f797f
messages.subject: Output datatable - Encoding
parts:
Hi all, 

I have a little problem with latin characters in my datatables. I´m using the read.delim function to read some tables that will be the output in my app. The characters "á,â,í,ó,ô,ç..." are � after reading the table.

My native encoding is latin1:
> localeToCharset()
[1] "ISO8859-1"

I´m a little bit confused about what to do, should I change the encoding?

Thanks in advance!

Luis

messages.author: f9ca1b61adbcd6fb
messages.subject: Re: Output datatable - Encoding
parts:
Hi Luis,

You should use UTF-8 as encoding. Try convert using iconv if necessary. 

Kind regards. 
Marcio

messages.author: abfba400e574bac9
messages.subject: Re: Output datatable - Encoding
parts:
Hi Luís,

try to do this:


var1 <- sort(unique(test$var1))

var1 <- iconv(var1, from="WINDOWS-1252", to='UTF-8', mark=T)

And when you to make a text in ui.r you can try, for example:

conditionalPanel(condition="input.conditionedPanels==3",
                     helpText(toUTF8("O Cruzeiro será o Campeão Brasileiro de 2014", "WINDOWS-1252"))
                     
                     )

Regards

Bruno Vidigal

messages.author: f9ca1b61adbcd6fb
messages.subject: Re: Output datatable - Encoding
parts:
Hi Luis, 

An alternative to Bruno solution is using encoding instead fileEncoding according to read.delim manual.

test<-read.delim("test.txt",sep="\t",dec=",",header=TRUE, encoding="UTF-8") or
test<-read.table(file = "test.txt", dec = ",", fileEncoding = "utf-8")

Kind regards,

Marcio
